Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER-Plus) accession framework

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin / issuing identity authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, signatories, UBOs and beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list and the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit's domestic watchlist. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) require Enhanced Due Diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening is conducted at onboarding, before name clearance, and on a continuous risk-triggered basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations online entity search and name clearance portal (MIRC corporate registry system, administered by the Registrar of Corporations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in the English/Latin alphabet; may include numerals and permitted punctuation; must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name in the Marshall Islands; no transliteration into Marshallese script is required, but all filings are accepted in English; names containing restricted tokens require prior written approval from the Registrar and, where applicable, the competent sectoral authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the Registrar of Corporations within 21 days of the rejection notice, setting out the grounds of distinctiveness and compliance. The Registrar must issue a written decision within 14 business days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may petition the High Court for judicial review. A rejected name may not be reused unless subsequently approved; name reservations may be extended for one additional 30-day period upon payment of the prescribed extension fee before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a non-resident business corporation; the registered office may consist of the licensed Registered Agent's physical street address in the Marshall Islands. No local employees, local premises, or physical operational presence are required for the bulk grain and soybean brokerage activity, provided the registered agent maintains corporate records and accepts service of process at the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5% in the ordinary course; unannounced on-site inspections are possible if the Financial Intelligence Unit or Registrar receives a suspicious transaction report, judicial request, or credible AML/CFT compliance deficiency, in which case inspection would focus primarily on the registered agent's books, UBO records, and transaction documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, 1990 (Rev. Cod. Tit. 20), Part II – Formation and Incorporation, Sections 20-201 to 20-211; Section 20-101 (Definitions); Section 20-122 (Registered Agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Authorized capital as set in Articles; shares may be issued for any lawful consideration as determined by the Board; no escrow requirement or capital deposit is mandated for non-resident business corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation hereby accepts the initial subscription of one thousand (1,000) shares of no-par value common stock issued to the incorporator, for a total consideration of $1,000, receipt of which is acknowledged and the shares are deemed fully paid. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at the office of its registered agent as stated in the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED, that the incorporator, John Doe, is appointed Sole Director; Jane Doe, President; and Richard Roe, Secretary-Treasurer, each to serve until successors are elected. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts and execute all documents to effectuate the Corporation's lawful purpose.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Registered Agent Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (online and in person, Majuro)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the Registrar's e-portal or paper form; verify name availability against the register of active business corporations; appoint a licensed registered agent in the Marshall Islands to accept service of process; the agent's consent form is required.
required_dossiers: Certificate of good standing of the proposed agent (if not previously filed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternate name list with three permitted alternates; if the agent is unqualified, substitute a licensed registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator / Corporate Services Provider; notarization by Marshall Islands Notary Public or consular officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation in English stating corporate name, registered office and registered agent, purpose (all lawful acts) or specific purpose, authorized share structure, and any limits on powers; execute Articles by the incorporator; have execution notarized or acknowledged; obtain the notarial certificate.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered agent
Incorporator's due diligence documents (passport, proof of address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a technical defect, amend the Articles and re-execute within the cure period; pay re-filing fee if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Payment at the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles with the government filing fee ($500) and any registered agent fee via electronic transfer, bank draft, or accepted payment method; obtain a stamped receipt and filing confirmation.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent (if not already filed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond within 15 business days by correcting the deficient page and filing an amendment; failure to cure may result in abandonment without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Post-Formation Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation; the registered agent obtains the certified copy; then prepare corporate records (by-laws, directors' consent, share ledger) and hold the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent adopting the first board resolutions.
required_dossiers: Minutes or unanimous written consent of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, file a Certificate of Correction under the BCA; if the registry loses documents, apply for a certified duplicate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax-Exempt/Non-Resident Status and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations and financial institution (selected bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a Statement of Non-Resident Status or incorporate as a non-resident business corporation; obtain the tax exemption certificate from the Ministry of Finance Revenue Office; open a corporate account with a licensed bank by presenting the formation package; obtain the corporate tax identification number if needed.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account opening forms and beneficial ownership declaration
Due diligence documents of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening, provide amended corporate records or select an alternate licensed bank; if tax exemption is refused, appeal to the Minister of Finance within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial licensing regime applies to commodity brokerage activities under ISIC 4631.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (no physical handling, storehouse, or warehouse operations).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – non-industrial activity; no EIA or registration required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – brokerage uses a registered office and does not generate effluent, VOCs, or solid waste; compliance with the Marshall Islands Clean Air and Clean Water Regulations is irrelevant due to zero onsite activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable – no physical premises, no employees operating from a workplace; no fire safety certificate or occupational safety clearance is required for the registered-agent office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance & Administration, Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Revenue and Taxation Office, Majuro; corporate registry portal operated by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations via International Registries, Inc. (www.register-rmi.com)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Business Corporation is not required to obtain a separate tax identification number unless it derives income from business carried on within the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The statutory identifier is the unique corporate registration number issued by the Registrar of Corporations upon incorporation through a licensed registered agent. If RMI-source business activity is subsequently commenced, the entity must register with the Revenue and Taxation Office under the Gross Revenue Tax regime, obtain a Gross Revenue Tax account number, and file quarterly returns. Foreign corporations with no RMI nexus are not subject to Gross Revenue Tax or income tax, and their only periodic obligation is the annual corporate franchise fee paid to the Registrar of Corporations. The local currency for any RMI-denominated filings is the United States Dollar (USD).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None available. The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not impose a national income tax on non-resident Business Corporations and therefore no check-the-box, entity-classification, or hybrid mismatch election exists under RMI law. The tax-exempt status is automatic and applies by operation of law to a Business Corporation that does not carry on business within the territorial limits of the Republic. No tax exemption certificate or special application procedure is required. An entity that wishes to maintain full non-resident status must simply refrain from engaging in RMI-source activities and must comply with corporate registry formalities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT or GST regime. The RMI does not impose a value-added tax, goods and services tax, or general sales and use tax. The only indirect-style impositions are customs import duties levied under the Customs and Excise legislation and the 3% Gross Revenue Tax applicable only to persons carrying on business within the Marshall Islands. Non-resident offshore entities engaged in the brokerage of bulk agricultural commodities are outside the scope of both regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable. There is no VAT/GST registration threshold in the Marshall Islands because no such tax exists. The 3% Gross Revenue Tax applies to any person 'engaged in business' within the RMI without a statutory monetary threshold, but an entity with no RMI-source activity is not registrable. If the entity becomes an employer of RMI-resident workers, registration with the RMI Social Security Administration is required from the date of first employment. All monetary references are in USD.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The Marshall Islands does not mandate electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API integration, or digital stamping. Conventional paper or PDF invoices are accepted for business recordkeeping purposes. The Revenue and Taxation Office retains the power to require production of books, records, invoices, bills of lading, and bank statements during audit or investigation proceedings.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Because the Marshall Islands has no VAT or GST, there is no 0% export VAT rate, no output tax to charge, and no input VAT credit to claim. The relevant relief for a non-resident Business Corporation is the automatic exclusion from the 3% Gross Revenue Tax and from RMI territorial income taxation in respect of profits derived outside the Republic. For goods in transit through RMI ports, no export duty is levied, and bunkers and ship supplies may be cleared duty-free where properly declared for export. Brokerage commissions earned from offshore bulk soybean and yellow corn chartering transactions have no RMI indirect tax consequence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: RMI Customs Export Declaration (Customs manifest covering the commodity voyage)
Ocean Bill of Lading or Charter Party Bill of Lading evidencing the shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit advice evidencing receipt of the export proceeds)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no VAT export-refund mechanism and therefore no VAT clawback exposure in the Marshall Islands. However, a false customs export declaration, misdescription of goods, or unauthorized transshipment can result in forfeiture of the goods, administrative pecuniary penalties, interest on any evaded duty, and criminal prosecution under the RMI Customs and Excise legislation. For entities within the Gross Revenue Tax net, fraudulent under-reporting can give rise to retrospective assessments, penalty surcharges, and cancellation of the corporate registration by the Registrar of Corporations. Non-resident status is not a shield against the consequences of misrepresenting RMI-source activity or customs documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) does not maintain a central bank and has no statutory foreign-exchange administration; the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender. Supervisory authority for banking and deposit-taking business rests with the Banking Commission of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (established under the Banking Act 1991), acting in coordination with the Ministry of Finance and the Financial Intelligence Office on AML/CFT and cross-border wire oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMI imposes no exchange-control legislation; because the U.S. dollar is domestic legal tender, current-account flows (trade settlements, freight, brokerage commissions) and capital-account flows (equity injections, shareholder loans, dividend and profit repatriation) are fully convertible by law without licensing, surrender, or prior regulatory approval. Practical gatekeeping is delegated to commercial banks and their correspondent banks, which apply AML/CFT due diligence, FATCA/CRS reporting, sanctions screening, and Beneficial Ownership verification; profit remittance is therefore unfettered once the remitting bank is satisfied as to source of funds, economic substance, and the underlying trade documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. RMI law stipulates no statutory repatriation window and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; grain-sale receivables may be collected and retained in USD either in the RMI or in offshore correspondent accounts. Covered financial institutions must nevertheless retain trade, wire-transfer, and KYC documentation for at least five years pursuant to the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, so a complete audit trail of the underlying charter party, bill of lading, sale confirmation, and payment instruction should be maintained.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Demand Deposit Account / Commercial Current Account with optional Capital Escrow sub-ledger
USD Commercial Operational Account with cross-border SWIFT wire and documentary LC services
Development-Finance Escrow Account - not suitable for commodity-trading treasury flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with conditions. The Banking Act 1991 reserves deposit-taking and banking business to licensed entities, and the RMI does not issue fintech EMI charters; however, an RMI-incorporated BC may lawfully open payment accounts with foreign-regulated digital EMI platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie, or similar cross-border payment institutions) provided such providers do not carry on regulated banking business in or from RMI territory. Practical constraints are substantial: EMIs apply enhanced institutional due diligence to RMI entities owing to the jurisdiction's offshore financial-center profile and FATF/APG mutual-evaluation monitoring history; onboarding typically requires certified corporate documents, director personal KYC with video interview, an explicit economic-substance narrative for ISIC 4631 agri-commodity brokerage, and a commitment to invoice- or LC-linked payment flows rather than unstructured third-party transfers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RMI law does not mandate universal in-person appearance; the AML/CFT framework permits equivalent non-face-to-face verification with a compulsory videoconference interview for non-resident directors. In practice, BOMI requires at least one director or signatory to attend a face-to-face due-diligence interview in Majuro or at a recognized consular office, whereas Bank of Guam normally permits remote onboarding upon receipt of notarized and apostilled board resolutions, certified passports of directors and UBOs, a Beneficial Ownership register, and a compliance-approved video call. A fully paperless, no-presence opening is therefore contingent on bank-specific risk appetite and the completeness of the corporate documentation pack.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee-shareholder or vaguely documented beneficial-ownership chain; registered-agent 'off-the-shelf' packaging flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; full Beneficial Ownership register maintained at the registered agent; corporate group chart; notarized UBO passports and residential proofs; sworn declaration of direct and indirect ownership; board resolution appointing authorized bank signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdiction risk - RMI characterized as offshore/IBC domicile with FATF/APG enhanced-monitoring history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic-substance file comprising signed grain brokerage and charter-party agreements, ISIC 4631 business plan, warehouse receipts and bill-of-lading history, audited IFRS financial statements, five-year cash-flow forecast, registered-agent address confirmation, and a professional opinion demonstrating substantive agri-commodity intermediation rather than passive asset holding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and trade-based money-laundering risk in bulk agri-commodity lanes (Black Sea, Latin American origins, transshipment and co-loading scenarios).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening log covering all counterparties, vessel IMO numbers, conveyors, and end-users; contractual sanctions and anti-terrorism clauses; ISPS/SOLAS compliance certificates and vessel voyage history; SGS/Intertek/Cotecna inspection certificates; INCOTERMS and discharge-port audit trail; negative news and adverse-media search records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity or unstructured USD wire flows disproportionate to stated capital base, suggestive of money laundering or tax evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury-flow narrative matching each MT103 to an underlying letter of credit, commercial invoice, charter party, or disbursement instruction; segregated Capital Escrow and Operational ledgers; pre-agreed payment purpose codes; monthly reconciliation pack; external auditor confirmation; and retention of all trade documents and payment instructions for at least five years.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital should be injected as SWIFT MT103 USD wires to the capital-settlement account with the narrative 'Equity contribution - MH_BC - ISIC 4631 grain brokerage'; the receiving bank requires the corporate resolution, share subscription agreement, updated register of members, and UBO disclosure before crediting. Because the U.S. dollar is the domestic currency and the RMI has no balance-of-payments reporting mandate, no statutory purpose-code or approval regime applies; nonetheless, the wire reference should recite 'Capital injection - no goods movement' to avoid trade-mismatch flags. Intercompany loan capital should follow a signed facility agreement with arm's-length pricing, use the reference 'Intercompany loan disbursement', and be supported by the borrower's board resolution and an updated shareholder register to preserve the tax-exempt character of the BC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Open-account supplier settlements should clear via SWIFT MT103 (with MT202 cover) referencing the purchase contract and invoice number. For bulk soybean and yellow-corn cargoes, the preferred rail is an Irrevocable, Transferable documentary Letter of Credit issued over SWIFT MT700 (with MT707 for amendments), with the RMI BC as applicant and a top-tier confirming bank as paying or reimbursing bank. The credit must oblige presentation of the full grain-trade document set: commercial invoice, clean negotiable ocean bill of lading, official GIPSA (US-origin) or SGS/Bureau Veritas weight and quality certificates, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, marine cargo insurance policy, and mate's receipt or survey report; funds are then released via MT103/MT202 against a complying presentation, thereby preserving the trade-money-laundering audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (USD against trade currencies such as BRL, ARS, UAH, CNY, and JPY) - no RMI central-bank approval required
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in tier-2 or restricted currencies for hedging grain-corridor payables and receivables
FX swaps and tom/next swaps for short-dated USD liquidity positioning
Cross-currency swaps under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with negotiated Credit Support Annex for tenor-matched commodity contracts
Vanilla purchased FX options (USD calls and puts) to cap conversion cost while preserving upside participation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Corporate Renewal Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Entities Division, Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of $150 per month or part thereof; non-filing for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registrar, with loss of legal capacity and standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax / Maintenance Fee Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RMI Ministry of Finance and Registrar of Corporations (single consolidated payment via Business Entities Division)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due simultaneously with the Annual Report on 31 March; no separate filing accepted after that date without penalty
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid balance accrues interest at 1% per month; repeated non-payment for two consecutive years triggers certificate of dissolution and permanent strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Agent and Registered Office Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent licensed by the Marshall Islands Business Entities Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be confirmed and current as of 31 March annually; agent to file notice of any address change within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain continuing registered agent and registered office authority renders the corporation subject to Registrar-ordered administrative dissolution and impairs service of process and enforcement of legal rights.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for a non-resident Business Corporation under the Business Corporations Act 1990; an independent audit is statutorily required only if the corporation is licensed under the RMI Banking Act, insurance legislation, or if shareholders holding at least 10% of voting power demand an audit. A pure bulk-grain brokerage holding no physical operations is not subject to Registrar-imposed audit certification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No codified local GAAP in the Marshall Islands; financial statements, when prepared, must fairly reflect the corporation's financial condition and transactions, and may follow IFRS or US GAAP consistently; books must be kept in English or be available for translation into English.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public beneficial-ownership register or standalone annual UBO filing exists for an RMI Business Corporation. The corporation must maintain a current internal register of members and directors, and must notify the registered agent of any share transfer or change in beneficial control within 21 days. Such changes are reflected in the next annual report; until the change is recorded, the corporation may not pay dividends or other distributions attributable to the transferred shares.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members showing all share transfers and beneficial ownership details as known
Minute Book recording board and shareholder resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,000-$15,000 if shareholders institute a voluntary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a non-resident Business Corporation (BC): the RMI Income Tax Act 1989 assesses tax only on income derived from sources within the Marshall Islands; offshore bulk-grain and soybean brokerage commission income earned by an MH_BC falls entirely outside the RMI corporate tax net.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holiday or preferential deduction is required to achieve a 0% effective rate on foreign-source brokerage revenue; the regime also imposes no capital gains tax, no branch profits tax, no remittance tax, no withholding tax on distributions, and no payroll tax on non-resident employees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return exists for a non-resident BC. The sole recurring filing obligation is the BCCA Annual Report, submitted by the licensed Marshall Islands registered agent to the RMI Registrar of Corporations in Majuro, using the Registrar's prescribed annual-report form and filing channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due on or before each anniversary of the date of filing of the Articles of Incorporation; a late surcharge is triggered if the report and the US$200 filing fee are not delivered within 60 days after that anniversary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Name and File Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name stated in the Articles of Incorporation and the assigned RMI registration/file number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the precise English legal name used on Bills of Lading, charterparties and LC documentation; any character-set or abbreviation variance invalidates the report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Registered Agent in the Marshall Islands
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and physical street address of the licensed registered agent in Majuro.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A post-office box alone is insufficient; the agent must be a law firm or trust company admitted to practice in RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Address of the corporation's main executive office; may be outside the Marshall Islands (e.g., Singapore, Dubai, Geneva).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the real trading desk from which voyage charters and brokerage decisions are executed; a nominee address triggers substance reviews by correspondent banks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names and residential addresses of all directors and officers; the BCCA requires at least one natural-person director.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Avoid corporate or nominee-only directors; disclose actual controlling individuals to satisfy bank KYC and TIEA expectations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of authorized shares, par value, classes and issued shares outstanding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the share structure exactly as presented to the issuing LC bank; any bearer-share feature must be disclosed and is a red flag in ESG due diligence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: US$200 filing fee remitted together with the report.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay through the registered agent; retain the receipt as proof of good standing for annual bank account reviews.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing after 60 days past the anniversary attracts a US$100 surcharge; failure to file for two consecutive years allows the Registrar to administratively dissolve the BC. Reinstatement requires settlement of all arrears plus a US$200 reinstatement fee. A dissolved BC cannot validly hold letters of credit, enforce charterparty rights or sue in the RMI High Court, and no Certificate of Good Standing is available until reinstatement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - the RMI imposes no dividend withholding tax; a BC may declare and pay dividends by board resolution to any shareholder, resident or non-resident, with no deduction at source and no advance clearance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has no comprehensive double taxation agreements, so no treaty-relief filing or tax-residency certificate can be issued. Dividend relief is structural: foreign-source income of the BC is outside the RMI tax base and the distribution is untaxed, so no TRC or beneficial-ownership declaration is required. Where the shareholder's residence state taxes the dividend (e.g., US GILTI/Subpart F, EU CFC rules), the shareholder must rely on local foreign-tax-credit or CFC provisions; the RMI, upon request through the registered agent, will issue a Certificate of Good Standing and board records evidencing the BCCA solvency test supporting the dividend declaration. RMI tax information exchange agreements (with the US, Australia, New Zealand and Nordic partners) permit spontaneous exchange of financial records with foreign tax authorities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest paid by an MH_BC. Because the RMI has no DTA network, treaty-reduced rates are not applicable; the domestic 0% rate already eliminates source taxation, leaving the recipient's residence jurisdiction as the sole taxing authority.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No RMI transfer-pricing statute, Local File, or Master File obligation exists for a BC (the RMI uses the US dollar). Nevertheless, for foreign-tax protection and bank due diligence, any intercompany brokerage, demurrage, freight or commission transaction exceeding US$100,000 per counterparty per year should be supported by written contracts, arm's-length commission-rate benchmarking (e.g., Baltic Exchange fixture data for the relevant grain route), voyage P&L evidence, and settlement exclusively via the target rails (Irrevocable Transferable LC / SWIFT wire).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI, as part of commitments accepted by the EU, has enacted economic substance requirements for non-resident domestic corporations. Bulk-vessel brokerage of agricultural soybeans and yellow corn constitutes a distribution and service centre type relevant activity, requiring: (i) direction and management of the brokerage business within the Marshall Islands, (ii) adequate physical premises and qualifying employees in RMI, (iii) performance of core income-generating activities (contract negotiation, voyage verification, demurrage resolution) in RMI, and (iv) annual substance filing. Non-compliance triggers fixed penalties, periodic default penalties, automatic exchange of information with EU and OECD partner tax authorities, and re-listing as a no-or-only-nominal-tax jurisdiction. The RMI remains engaged in FATF/APG follow-up; UBO transparency and demonstrated substance are essential to preserve correspondent banking access for LC and SWIFT settlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-Border Tax Evasion and Abusive Conduit Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the MH_BC as an invoice pass-through or LC-settlement shell with no genuine brokerage function, or concealing commission income from the shareholder's residence tax authority while claiming RMI 0% taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the RMI Income Tax Act 1989 for false declarations and information-exchange obstruction; in the shareholder's residence state, CFC/GILTI or controlled-foreign-company rules, CRS/FATCA/DAC-6 reporting consequences, recharacterization of income, interest on back taxes, accuracy penalties up to 200% of the understated commission income, and criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil where the BC is a mere façade, holding directors and shareholders personally liable for the foreign tax, penalties and interest; personal prosecution, cross-border travel bans, and extradition under mutual legal assistance and TIEA channels are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Nominee-only directors, no documented board meetings, no RMI premises or staff, no records evidencing negotiation of charterparties or freight rates, and failure to file the BCCA Annual Report for two consecutive years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution by the Registrar; reinstatement requires payment of all arrears plus a US$200 reinstatement fee. The dissolved BC's bank accounts are frozen by the correspondent bank, EU/OECD defensive measures are triggered, and grain suppliers may terminate agreements for material breach of warranty of good standing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors become personally liable for all debts and contractual obligations (including freight, demurrage and cargo claims) incurred in the name of the dissolved corporation, as the BCCA liability shield ceases; personal exposure enforced before the RMI High Court and foreign courts via judgment recognition.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Brokering soybean or corn cargoes to or from OFAC/EU/UN-sanctioned jurisdictions, using blocked vessels or SDN-listed counterparties, structuring payments below reporting thresholds, or concealing the ultimate beneficial owner to evade TIEA queries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under the Money Laundering Control Act 2003 (as amended) with criminal fines and imprisonment up to the statutory maximum, civil forfeiture of commissions and cargo, revocation of the registered agent's license to act for the entity, prohibition from any RMI-licensed banking relationship, and UN/EU asset freezes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate face individual criminal liability, personal OFAC civil penalties per violation transmitted through the US clearing system, travel bans, freezing of personal assets, and extradition; personal net worth is exposed to civil restitution in favor of charterers, issuing banks and joint-venture victims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining bearer shares, refusing to disclose beneficial owners on bank KYC forms, or destroying broker journals, email records and voyage files requested by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit or a TIEA partner such as the US, Australia or New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and penalties under RMI AML regulations and the TIEA framework, adverse inference in foreign tax proceedings, termination of LC/SWIFT banking relationships, inclusion on financial-action risk lists, and effective commercial exclusion from international grain commodity trading.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who certify false UBO declarations face fines, imprisonment, and disqualification from serving as directors of any RMI entity; civil liability extends to the full losses suffered by charterers, banks and joint-venture partners that relied on the false declaration.
